passage:
"Gopika, just show me question five. Please."
"Arnab, I can't. It's a test."
"You're so selfish. Everyone shares."
"I'm not sharing, and I'm not trying to be mean."
"Priya said you'd say that. She said you think you're better than us."
"I don't. I'm tired of feeling guilty for saying no, though." She breathed out. "Look, I'll study with you after school today. We can go through the chapter together, and you can ask me anything before the test."
"That's not the same."
"I know. But it's what I can do."
Arnab scowled and turned away. Gopika's hands were shaking, but she stayed where she was and opened her notebook.

qa.q: Which question did Arnab ask Gopika to show?
How does Gopika feel about refusing, and what shows it?
qa.a: She feels guilty and nervous but firm. She says she is tired of feeling guilty for saying no, and her hands were shaking.

qa.q: What did Gopika offer instead of sharing answers?
qa.a: To study with Arnab after school, going through the chapter together so Arnab could ask her anything before the test.

qa.q: Why might Arnab react with anger even though Gopika offered help?
qa.a: Arnab wanted the answers now, and studying is more work. Arnab may also be afraid of failing, which could explain the scowl and turning away.

grounding: A classmate is pressured to share answers, refuses kindly, offers to study together and accepts some anger.

passage:
I'm Noor, and I used to think being liked meant saying yes. Then came the take-home economics test in Class 11. The night before it was due, the class group lit up: "Noor send ur answers pls," "just the long ones," "don't be selfish yaar." Sarika even called and said everyone would hate me if I didn't.

I typed "okay" three times and deleted it three times. My chest felt tight. In the end I wrote, "I can't share answers, it's a graded test. But I'm free at seven. Anyone who wants to go over chapter four with me can join a call."

A few people left the group chat in protest. Someone posted an eye-roll. But at seven, Sarika joined, and two others. We worked through supply curves until nine. Sarika said, "Okay, this actually makes sense now." Not everyone forgave me. I could live with that.

qa.q: What time did Noor offer to go over chapter four?
qa.a: Noor offered to go over chapter four at seven.

qa.q: Why did Noor keep typing "okay" and deleting it?
qa.a: Noor felt pressured and afraid of being disliked, so part of Noor wanted to give in, but Noor also felt it would be wrong to share a graded test.
Refusing kindly while offering a study call worked, because it kept the test fair and still gave classmates real help.

qa.q: What was it like for Sarika to join the call after pushing Noor?
qa.a: Sarika may have felt a bit embarrassed after the pressure Sarika put on Noor, but also relieved and grateful once the chapter finally made sense.

grounding: It shows a teen pressed by classmates to share answers and called selfish, who refuses kindly, offers to study together and accepts some anger.

passage:
Lab in-charge's note, Chemistry, Term 2 practicals

On Wednesday I stepped into the prep room and found a small crowd around Bhupen's bench. His practical record book was the only complete one in the section. Salma was holding it out of his reach, saying, "Just let us copy the readings, don't be so stingy, we're a class, na?" Others were nodding.

Bhupen reached for the book, red in the face, and said quietly, "I'm not giving the readings. You'll get caught, and so will I. But I'll come early tomorrow and help anyone redo the titrations." Salma rolled her eyes and told him he was selfish. A couple of them muttered on the way out.

I did not step in at once because he was handling it. Afterwards I told him the prep room is open at 8 a.m. and I would supervise. Next morning, five students came, including Salma, who stayed quiet but finished her readings.

qa.q: What did Salma want to copy from Bhupen's record book?
qa.a: Salma wanted to copy the readings.

qa.q: What does Bhupen's red face suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: His red face suggests he felt embarrassed and cornered by the crowd, even though he kept his voice quiet and firm.

qa.q: How did the lab in-charge support Bhupen's choice?
qa.a: The lab in-charge opened the prep room at 8 a.m. and offered to supervise, making Bhupen's offer to help redo the titrations possible.

qa.q: How might Salma see the next morning's session?
qa.a: Salma may have felt awkward after calling Bhupen selfish, which may explain why she stayed quiet, but she still came and got her own readings done.

grounding: It shows a teen pressured by classmates to share answers and called selfish, who refuses kindly and offers to help them study instead.
